subject: Q4 GPU tranche arbitration — HelioBio vs Mosaic AI
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Q4 GPU tranche arbitration — HelioBio vs Mosaic AI

Team,

We have a tranche conflict for the West-2 dedicated pool (cluster-w2-ded). Two committed deals overlap for the same Q4 window and the available A100-equivalent capacity has been reduced by the planned maintenance (finalized last week). Quick facts: 

- HelioBio (DL-9834) — Reserved: 8 A100-equivalent slots, committed start 2026-12-05, revenue ARR weight high, SLA: 99.9% latency SLO.
- Mosaic AI (DL-9991) — Reserved: 6 A100-equivalent slots, committed start 2026-12-01, ARR weight medium, SLA: 99.5%.
- Current usable capacity in cluster-w2-ded for that window: 10 A100-equivalent slots (maintenance reduces nominal 14 -> 10).

We need an allocation decision by EOD today so we can notify customers and implement routing/fallbacks. Options I see (ranked roughly by business impact):

1) Prioritize by committed ARR and SLA — allocate 8 to HelioBio, 2 to Mosaic; offer Mosaic a staged activation (burst windows outside HelioBio peak) + 15% credit for inconvenience.
2) Time-segment the tranche — give HelioBio mornings (8 slots) and Mosaic afternoons (6 slots) with an overlap window transiently oversubscribed (will use preemption rules).
3) Short-term borrow 4 slots from Hosted pool for Mosaic for first 30 days (operational risk but lower customer impact).
4) Request both PMs to accept a 20% reduction in initial committed throughput for the first 30 days while we finish capacity ramp (revenue impact).

Attachments: DL-9834-deal-summary.pdf, capacity_timeline_q4.csv (two attachments) — see revenue / SLO details.

Please reply with your recommendation and the operational steps you would need (routing changes, preemption config, host-borrow runbook). I know this is messy; want a defensible, customer-facing decision.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 GPU tranche arbitration — HelioBio vs Mosaic AI
Jordan —

Thanks for the summary. Quick data point from Console: HelioBio's token-volume profile indicates peak usage between 14:00-18:00 UTC (mornings PST), Mosaic's peak is 00:00-08:00 UTC (evening PST). That gives us a windowing opportunity (option 2) that would cover both peaks with minimal overlap. 

However, two caveats:
- The revenue weight for HelioBio is higher (confirmed) and they have escalation clauses tied to latency in the contract — losing headroom for them exposes us to credit triggers.
- Mosaic runs a short daily heavy-batch job that cannot be trivially throttled without impacting their upcoming evaluation run (they flagged an internal deadline).

Operational ask if we do time-segmenting: we need to add a per-customer routing rule (time-of-day) and a soft-preempt policy for the 1-hour overlap window. Marcus, can you confirm the effort to implement time-of-day routing and the expected SLO hit in the overlap?

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 GPU tranche arbitration — HelioBio vs Mosaic AI
Laura / Jordan —

Technical constraints to consider: 

- The cluster-w2-ded nodes are a mix of A100-40GB and A100-80GB; HelioBio's quantized runtime benefits more from 80GB availability. That limits us if we try straight slot swapping.
- Repacking (live-migrating customers between nodes to free homogeneous pods) will incur a 2–3 hour window where KV caches are cold and customers will see higher latency.

Suggested approach (combined):
1) Implement time-segmenting as Laura suggested for non-overlap hours (low dev effort — routing rule + token-tag window).
2) For the 2-hour overlap we run a short preemption policy: HelioBio keeps priority, Mosaic is routed to Hosted pool for up to 4 GPUs while we finish post-maintenance repacking. Hosted borrow is operationally feasible for 30 days but requires an immediate ops ticket and cost allocation.
Operational steps I need if approved:
- Create routing rules in Traffic Router (30m).
- Spin up Hosted pool VMs and re-route Mosaic (1–2 hours).
- Run repack playbook to optimize node placement overnight (3 hours, low-risk, requires rollback plan).
Downsides: Hosted borrow increases OPEX for December; repack can cause short tail-latency spikes.
I can draft a technical runbook for the above and an implementation window tonight if folks agree.
Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alexei Romanov <alexei.romanov@heliobio.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@mosaic.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 GPU tranche arbitration — HelioBio vs Mosaic AI
Jordan,

Appreciate the heads up but this is urgent on our side. Our validation runs for the week depend on steady 8-slot throughput — if our morning window gets reduced we risk missing milestones with our clinical partner. We signed for the 8-slot reserved commit and expect Redwood to honor the capacity, especially since HelioBio prioritized the earlier commitment in the contract negotiations.

If there's any chance to avoid routing us to Hosted or to time-segment our windows, please note that our evaluation run cannot be moved later than 2026-12-10. We will escalate to procurement/legal if this shifts our start.
— Alexei
Alexei Romanov
Head of ML Ops, HelioBio
alexei.romanov@heliobio.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, alexei.romanov@heliobio.com, procurement@mosaic.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 GPU tranche arbitration — HelioBio vs Mosaic AI
Team / Alexei / Mosaic procurement,
Thanks for the fast responses and context. Decision (executive summary):

1) Time-segmented routing (primary): We will implement time-of-day routing so HelioBio receives priority during their validated morning window (14:00-18:00 UTC). Mosaic will receive priority during their heavy-batch window (00:00-08:00 UTC). This minimizes direct overlap and preserves both customers' critical runs.

2) Overlap handling (1.5 hours per day): HelioBio retains priority in the overlap. Mosaic will be temporarily routed to Hosted pool for up to 4 GPUs during that overlap for the first 14 calendar days, after which we expect repack to complete and re-evaluate.

3) Credits and communications: Because this is an operational disruption, Mosaic will get a 12% service credit for December; HelioBio will receive a 5% credit for the partial migration risk and a named escalation contact (Laura).
4) Next steps (owners):
- Marcus: create time-of-day routing rule + run repack playbook tonight (start 19:00 PST). Estimate completion 23:00 PST.
- Monica: draft customer comms for HelioBio + Mosaic and include the runbook excerpt and mitigation timeline (send by 19:30 PST).
- Laura: be primary escalation contact for HelioBio; coordinate legal if HelioBio pushes for contract remedies.
I will notify both accounts and open the Hosted borrow ops ticket immediately. We will track this as an SLA-impacting incident in PagerDuty with incident code PD-2026-1129-TRANCHE and log credits in Billing.
Attachments: escalation_resolution.md (short decision note)
Alexei — I know this is not ideal. We chose the approach that minimizes revenue and experiment disruption across both customers while keeping a rollback path. Laura will be your point-of-contact for any contract escalation.
I'll follow up tomorrow with the post-repack validation plan.
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
